answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must contact MSHA immediately, and within 15 minutes, once it knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes once it knows or should know of an accident involving a death at the mine.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where rock dust is required, the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. When methane is absent, no increase is added to that figure.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The increase applies only where methane is present in a ventilating current (0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane).
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Under 30 CFR 75.1714, the operator must make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Underground metal/nonmetal mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties (30 CFR 48.5). The chunks don't label which part covers underground miners. I treated § 48.5 as the underground rule because it requires training under conditions that duplicate underground conditions and requires self-rescue training before a new miner goes underground.

claims.text: Section 48.5 requires each new miner to receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.answer: The provided chunks do not state the numeric permissible exposure level (PEL) as an 8-hour average. The definitions chunk is cut off before the PEL definition.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 and 57.9300. Those are the surface and underground metal and nonmetal sections. Berms may have openings as needed for roadway drainage.

claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in 57.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms may have openings to the extent necessary for roadway drainage.
claims.quote: Berms may have openings to the extent necessary for roadway drainage.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
